stories.title: Your AI agent fixed the bug, but what else did it change?
stories.reason: Trail of Bits shipped two open-source Codex plugins with a genuinely new verification method (three-arm proof: fails on original, passes on patch, fails again on revert) and measured false-positive reduction on real PRs — running code, concrete numbers, AI x cyber square in the brief.
key_facts: patching-bugs requires a three-arm proof: same repro fails on original code, passes on patched code, fails again once the patch is reverted
regression-hunt: diff->callers->live repro->fresh-context replay->adjudication agent, 4-step pipeline
regression-hunt had 25% fewer false positives than a baseline Codex agent (95% CI 14-38%)
Review of 130+ merged PRs found 21 confirmed regressions (16 functional, 1 perf, 4 build/test), none security
Open source: github.com/trailofbits/skills, plugins patching-bugs and regression-hunt

stories.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Leads Benchmarks for Finding, Exploiting, and Patching Vulnerabilities
stories.reason: Gemini 4 Carbon's launch leads with new, numbered cybersecurity-eval results (SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym, CWE-bench) rather than a generic capability bump — exactly the security-benchmark category Mine always-surfaces.
key_facts: SEC-bench Pro: 88.2% for finding vulnerabilities
ExploitGym: 54.8% for exploitation
CWE-bench: 71.0% for patching
Google says Carbon is twice as likely to generate secure code vs predecessor Argon
Access initially limited to a subset of cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program
Google says it resisted every evaluated indirect prompt-injection attempt

stories.title: Grace Blackwell needs a new scheduler: 27% more usable GPUs from the same racks
stories.reason: Concrete GPU-serving/scheduling infra story with hard numbers across multiple benchmarks (rack fragmentation, defragmentation, serving throughput) — exactly the 'how models are served' lane Mine weights above training.
key_facts: NVL72 racks: only rack-local multi-node jobs get full NVLink speedup; cross-rack falls back to slower InfiniBand
SkyPilot's topology-aware scheduler + defrag yields 27% more usable nodes on a 128-rack/2304-node model (2037 vs 1602 nodes) vs naive 18-node slicing
NVIDIA GR00T team measured 14.4% pre-training throughput gain (1.59s -> 1.39s/iter) from rack-aware placement
GB200 NVL72 w/ 32-way expert parallelism: up to 4.4x throughput/GPU vs 8-GPU B200 for DeepSeek-R1 serving
Estimated ~$16.7K/training-hour saved on a 10,000-GPU cluster

stories.title: Claude Code regularly sends each background agent’s transcript to its model
stories.reason: Concrete, reproducible finding about Claude Code's own architecture: background agents get a full-transcript 'describe your last action' call roughly every 30s, with no toggle, costing a measured 16-26% of a user's agent spend per independent reports (GitHub issue #86879). High HN resonance (562 pts) and directly actionable for anyone running background agents.
key_facts: Claude Code sends each background agent's full transcript to its model ~every 30s to generate a 3-5 word status line
No setting to disable it; on by default since v2.1.232 (Aug 2026)
Author's own telemetry: agent_summary calls were 16.4% of spend vs 15.7% for the main conversation before an unofficial patch; 0% after
GitHub issue #86879 cites four independent measurements of 18-26% of spend
Unofficial workaround: a Bun --preload script (no-agent-summary.js) that neutralizes the timer callback

stories.title: GitLab Security Incident: Attempted Exploitation of CVE-2026-97229
stories.reason: A critical (CVSS 10.0) GitLab regex-engine flaw was actively probed against Alpine Linux's own GitLab instance, forcing a full rebuild and password reset — a major pure-security incident (no AI angle) in widely-used container-ecosystem infrastructure, large enough to clear the pure-cyber headline bar.
key_facts: CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 10.0) is a regex-engine (Onigmo/Ruby) bug in how GitLab evaluates CI configs
Attacker crashed GitLab worker processes 8 times across Oct 20-26, got partway through the exploit chain 4 times
Alpine's initial patch (GitLab 19.3.5/19.3.6) didn't close the hole because its container image used unpatched upstream Ruby
No confirmed compromise, but logging gaps mean a successful exploit could have left no trace; instance rebuilt from scratch
All GitLab passwords reset; users told to re-pull the Oct 27 image and upgrade Ruby independently of GitLab

stories.title: Cloudflare links vulnerability discovery to defense with OpenAI
stories.reason: Primary-source (OpenAI) account of a real production deployment: Cloudflare uses OpenAI's Daybreak to investigate vulnerabilities and propose fixes for human review, plus Codex for dev work — concrete AI x cyber-defense use, though the full writeup was blocked (403) so detail is limited to the summary.
key_facts: Cloudflare uses OpenAI Daybreak to investigate vulnerabilities and propose fixes for review
Cloudflare developers use Codex to build faster and improve code quality

stories.title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities
stories.reason: OpenAI's 'Patch the Planet' coordinates security researchers, maintainers and incident responders around agent-surfaced open-source vulnerabilities — a real AI x cyber coordination mechanism, but the announcement page was blocked (403) so there are no hard numbers to confirm scale.
key_facts: Patch the Planet connects security researchers, maintainers, and incident responders to address critical open-source vulnerabilities agents uncover

stories.title: Sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning
stories.reason: Google Research's Sleep framework (wake/sleep consolidation on a Hope-architecture MoE) reports real benchmark numbers (near-zero forgetting on Manchu/Kalamang translation, BABILong to 10M tokens) but no code is released, and it's a training/continual-learning method rather than a serving concern Mine weights higher.
key_facts: Alternates a wake phase (handles inputs, stores temporary info) and a sleep phase (consolidates into long-term MoE params)
Near-zero forgetting on continual translation to unseen languages Manchu and Kalamang, where ICL/Cartridges/SFT suffered severe forgetting
Near-perfect BABILong scaling to 10M tokens, beating GPT-4 and Titans
SQuAD-style factual retention: 48.9% single-task, 46.2% continued pre-training
No code released; only an arXiv link (2606.03979)
